Subject: Spike in p95/p99 for long-input jobs (16k context)

Hi Rachel,

We're seeing a sudden spike in p95/p99 latency and an increase in 5xx errors on the hosted API when we send long-context jobs (mostly ~14k-18k token requests) using redwood-32k-v1. The degradation started around 07:40 PST and so far we've seen p95 climb from ~1.8s to >6s and p99s spike above 12s for many requests; a few calls are timing out. This is hitting user-facing flows for our document ingestion pipeline.

Example request IDs: bp-req-20270118-9421, bp-req-20270118-9460. We captured server-side traces and a sample payload — attaching brightpath-traces-0118.zip and sample-payload-14k.txt. Happy to jump on a call; this is high priority for us.

On Mon, Jan 18, 2027 at 08:28 AM Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Elena — thanks for the quick heads-up...

Quick triage summary from infra: we see a sharp increase in end-to-end latency correlated with requests that have sequence lengths > ~12k tokens. The traces show the following pattern:
- Large requests bypass prefix cache (misses) and force full KV-cache loads;
- Our batcher groups by model-only for a short window; when a very long sequence arrives it triggers kernel selection paths that are several orders slower for that step (quantized fallback combined with attention kernel change).
- When that slower path is taken, it occupies worker slots for an extended time, causing head-of-line blocking for other requests in the same pool and increasing p95/p99.

I've attached engine-trace-1692.json with correlation ids (we matched bp-req-20270118-9421). Preliminary mitigation we can do immediately (minutes):
1) Route BrightPath traffic to a separate pool with an enforced max_sequence_length=8192 for the hosted tier. This avoids fallback kernel path for the majority of their traffic.
2) Enable aggressive prefix caching for repeated prefixes (we can flip this in config for the account).
3) Temporarily disable streaming for long-context requests to reduce worker lock time; stream later when kernel path is stable.

These actions are low-risk and reversible. Longer-term fixes: revisit kernel selection heuristics, pre-warm quantized kernels for 16k+ sequences, and add per-tenant circuit-breakers that avoid head-of-line blocking.

I'll stand by on the call and can throttle or apply routing changes immediately if you approve.

—Evelyn Hart
SRE Lead, Runtime
evelyn@redwood.ai

Subject: Action plan and temporary mitigation (BrightPath traffic)

Hi Elena — quick status and immediate actions we just applied:
- We routed BrightPath traffic to an isolated pool with max_sequence_length=8192 (effective immediately).
- Enabled prefix caching aggressively for this account.
- Disabled streaming for requests > 8k tokens to reduce worker lock time.

Early signals: error rate has dropped ~60% and p95 is trending back toward the expected range for most requests. We will keep monitoring through the day.

Next steps (timeline):
- Today: monitoring + rollback guard (Evelyn on standby).
- 48 hours: performance postmortem + suggested route for long-term capacity (kernel pre-warm + dedicated pool options).
- We will share a postmortem doc and propose a credits package for the production impact.

Can you confirm you've seen immediate improvement on your side? We'll set a separate postmortem meeting for 48 hours.

—Rachel
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
